facts.raw_span: dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in the left prepectoral area
an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
antibiotics (amoxicillin–clavulanate, 1 g three times daily) were started empirically
A swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis
the lesion had darkened and enlarged

concepts.why: The patient developed an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site, and a swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, indicating a pacemaker pocket infection.
The patient's lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, and the lesion had darkened and enlarged despite antibiotic therapy, indicating a Staphylococcal device infection.
The patient developed an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site after pacemaker implantation, indicating a surgical site infection.
The patient had an elevated inflammatory syndrome, and the lesion had darkened and enlarged despite antibiotic therapy, indicating a device-related sepsis.
The patient's lesion had darkened and enlarged despite antibiotic therapy, indicating a chronic device infection.
The patient's lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, indicating bacterial colonization of the device.
The patient developed an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site after pacemaker implantation, indicating a postoperative wound infection.
The patient developed an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site, and a swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, indicating an implantable device-related infection.
It explains the 2:1 atrioventricular block finding in the vignette.

rationales.F03: Pacemaker implantation is a known risk factor for device-related infections.
rationales.F06: The presence of an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site is highly suggestive of a device-related infection.
rationales.F10: The growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis from a swab of the lesion is consistent with a device-related infection.
rationales.F12: The darkening and enlargement of the lesion despite antibiotic therapy suggests a severe infection.
